thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: rwd-serve-eu-1 experiencing high tail latency and OOMs across a subset of nodes. Paging on-call: @Sam :rotating_light:
pd-bot: Page routed to Sam (oncall) and Jakob (sre). Priority: P0.
Sam (oncall): ack, looking at dashboards now. Starting with top errors...
Sam (oncall): I see a huge spike in kv_cache_bytes for pool rwd-serve-eu-1 starting 2024-03-12T09:10Z. Per-node memory jumped ~3.8GB above baseline.
Jakob (sre): saw repeated cudaMalloc failures in logs: "CUDA out of memory when allocating 2199023255552 bytes" (truncated) and fallback OOMs. Nodes show fragmentation (free large blocks very scarce).
Jo (engineer): also seeing continuous-batching queue depth climb from 5->200, batch latency up to 6s. Many requests are small sequences but KV entries are large variable sizes.
Maya (ml-runtime): probable KV cache blowup + allocator fragmentation. On top of that, our batcher is allowing large prefixes to be evaluated which creates huge KV entries and triggers ptorch allocator split behavior.
Ash (support): we have 3 customers reporting high latency, 1 reporting 502s and request timeouts. Triage: customer A (fintech) impacted worst.
Sam (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) throttle/disable continuous batching for pool, 2) force kv cache cap and eviction, 3) set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF to reduce fragmentation, 4) roll hotfix to batch config. I'll coordinate.
Jo (engineer): quick hotfix: POST to admin API to set max_batch_size and disable batching in the pool config:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.rw/api/pools/rwd-serve-eu-1/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"continuous_batching":false, "max_batch_size":8, "kv_cache_max_bytes":2000000000}'
```
Sam (oncall): applying now to all nodes in pool (canary 2 nodes first).
deploy-bot: config-change started for rwd-serve-eu-1 (canary nodes: n-12,n-13)
Sam (oncall): canary looks good: CPU and GPU mem freed, kv_cache_bytes per node down ~45%.
Maya (ml-runtime): while we do config changes, set env on instances: 
```
export TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.6,max_split_size_mb:128
```
This stops allocator from holding lots of tiny free blocks and encourages coalescing. Also set REDWOOD_KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=2000000000 temporarily.
Jakob (sre): also running a rolling restart of the worker process on nodes that hit the worst fragmentation (n-05,n-08,n-21). Restart forces allocator reset.
Sam (oncall): rolling restart started. Expect transient 5-10s interruptions per worker. Notifying support to warn customers.
Ash (support): customer messages sent to impacted accounts: acknowledging incident, mitigation in progress, ETA ~20-40min.
deploy-bot: config-change rollout progress: 25% -> 60% -> 100% (complete)
Jakob (sre): after restarts and TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF set, cudaMalloc failures dropped to zero, p99 latency back to baseline ~120ms, tail latency now ~1s.
Maya (ml-runtime): root cause hypothesis: KV cache fragmentation + allocator behavior when continuous batching exposes many variable-length KV writes. Small sequences + long prefixes create many heterogenous KV allocations; PyTorch/CUDA allocator splits blocks and leaves fragmented holes. Batcher backpressure permitted large concurrent in-flight KV inserts, making fragmentation worse.
Jo (engineer): short term follow-ups: 1) keep continuous_batching disabled for pool until comfortable, 2) enforce kv_cache_max_bytes + LRU eviction, 3) add admission control (reject huge prefixes under low-mem), 4) instrument per-request kv allocation size metric.
Sam (oncall): handing off to Maya for next steps and postmortem. My oncall ends in 30m.
Maya (ml-runtime): taking over. I'll run further analysis: heap snapshots, per-request kv histogram, and a stress test that simulates small-seq-many-large-prefix pattern. I'll also prepare a patch to allocator arena sizing and consider a tuned arena via TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF or a custom small-block allocator.
Ash (support): current customer impact: 3 customers degraded, 1 transient 502. No billing anomalies reported.
Jakob (sre): logs and relevant slices pushed to incident ticket #INC-4892. Tagging teams: eng-runtime, eng-ml, eng-sre.
Maya (ml-runtime): follow-up action items (short):
- Create RFC for arena tuning + default TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF (owner: Maya)
- Add a canary test for continuous_batching behavior with kv-heavy prefixes (owner: Jo)
- Add eviction thresholds per-model and per-pool (owner: Sam)
- Postmortem scheduled tomorrow 10:00 UTC (organizer: Sam)
Sam (oncall): thanks everyone. Closing pager and marking incident as mitigated. If anything regresses, @channel. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: rwd-serve-eu-1 - mitigation applied, p99 restored. Postmortem required.
